Bayesian model-averaged BMD with the EFSA defaults

Source: R/efsa.R
bmdefsa.Rd

Fits the models of the Bayesian benchmark dose modelling of EFSA (2022) available in drcTMB, in the BMD parameterisation with the priors of efsapriors, for each model and family, and averages them by bmdbayes.

Usage

bmdefsa(
  form,
  data,
  bmr = NULL,
  def = NULL,
  models = NULL,
  family = c("gaussian", "lognormal"),
  ...,
  prior.weights = NULL,
  method = c("is", "laplace"),
  n = 5000,
  df = 4,
  control = list()
)

Arguments

form, data

formula and data, as in drmTMB

bmr, def

the benchmark response and its definition (see efsapriors)

models

the models (see efsapriors), by default all: six for continuous responses, and eight, including probit and logit, for quantal responses

family

the families: for continuous responses "gaussian" and "lognormal" (both by default), for quantal responses "binomial"

...

further arguments of efsapriors: background, maxresponse, bmd, dprior, extended

prior.weights, method, n, df

see bmdbayes; prior weights in the order of the fits, for each model the families, labelled model_N (gaussian), model_LN (lognormal) and model_Q (binomial), e.g. weibull2_N, weibull2_LN, weibull1_N, .... The default method is importance sampling ("is"): with the PERT priors, the posterior modes are often close to a bound of a prior, e.g. a background close to 0, where the Laplace approximation is poor.

control

a list of control parameters of drmTMB

Value

a bmdbayes object, with the fits (fits) and the priors (efsa) of the models; models whose fit fails are left out with a warning

Details

The data requirements are those of efsapriors.

References

EFSA Scientific Committee (2022). Guidance on the use of the benchmark dose approach in risk assessment. EFSA Journal 20(10), 7584.

See also

efsapriors, bmdbayes, fitpert, TCDD, liver.tumor

Examples

# \donttest{
# quantal: liver tumours after exposure to TCDD
set.seed(1)
(ba <- bmdefsa(cbind(incidence, total - incidence) ~ conc, data = TCDD, family = "binomial"))
#> Bayesian model-averaged benchmark dose, excess risk 0.1, prior pert(0, 19.28, 115.68, shape=0.0001) for the BMD
#> Importance sampling
#> 
#>                     model   family  logML prior  weight  ess    BMD  BMDL  BMDU
#> weibull2_Q       weibull2 binomial -13.24 0.125 0.13971 3045  9.517 4.004 20.93
#> weibull1_Q       weibull1 binomial -13.84 0.125 0.07622 3679  7.835 3.969 15.79
#> loglogistic_Q loglogistic binomial -13.05 0.125 0.16843 3454  8.948 3.873 19.70
#> lognormal_Q     lognormal binomial -13.74 0.125 0.08462 3323  8.628 4.022 18.80
#> gamma_Q             gamma binomial -13.17 0.125 0.14976 2799  9.947 4.204 20.99
#> multistage_Q   multistage binomial -12.51 0.125 0.28948 4044 12.766 8.055 21.82

#> logit_Q             logit binomial -14.50 0.125 0.03953 1832 12.965 5.363 26.20
